exam.title: CompTIA Security+ (V7)
exam.study_prerequisites: CompTIA recommends Network+ knowledge and two years in a security or systems-administrator role. Practice control/risk mapping, PKI, secure architecture and data/resilience decisions, baselines/IAM/vulnerability management, monitoring/detection, incident/forensic evidence, governance/risk/third parties/audit, and awareness in isolated or explicitly authorized environments. Verify scheduling against the June 11, 2027 English retirement or August 13, 2027 Japanese, Portuguese, Spanish, and Thai retirement; no successor is inferred.

review.notes: All five weighted V7 domains are connected through an asset, risk, control, evidence, response, recovery and governance lifecycle, with three scenarios, eight isolated/authorized labs and 42 original checks. The guide records CompTIA's exact June 11, 2027 English and August 13, 2027 Japanese/Portuguese/Spanish/Thai retirement dates without inferring a successor. All eight guide URLs are cataloged: six reachable and O'Reilly plus Udemy automation-blocked; none missing or broken. No proprietary objectives, PBQs, course labs, leaked drafts or recalled items are used. September 27, 2026: checked version-specific V7 and announced V8 citations and reconciled link counts; historical full-review date and objective snapshot retained.

findings.title: One answer was stale after the published successor announcement
findings.evidence: The guide transition section already named V8/SY0-801, but answer 42 still said not to infer a successor.
findings.recommendation: State the explicit expected November 17, 2026 announcement and keep SY0-701 language-specific retirement and current scope separate.

findings.title: Certificate-path and revocation checks have different evidence
findings.evidence: The selected verifier uses explicit roots, time and expected DNS identity; a separate CRL is not automatically consumed.
findings.recommendation: Add original executed path/CSR tests and separate signed-CRL checks with an explicit revocation limitation.
findings.resolution: Add original executed path/CSR tests and separate signed-CRL checks with an explicit revocation limitation.

findings.title: Zero-trust policy decisions and enforcement need separate roles
findings.evidence: NIST section 3 distinguishes policy engine, administrator and enforcement point, also named in PDF objective 1.2.
findings.recommendation: Teach the three roles and an original contractor-access decision/enforcement case.
findings.resolution: Teach the three roles and an original contractor-access decision/enforcement case.

findings.title: Current incident response guidance differs in organization from exam milestones
findings.evidence: Revision 3 section 2.1 aligns response to CSF 2.0 while broader preparation and continuous improvement support it.
findings.recommendation: Retain objective 4.8 milestones and explicitly label current operational context; no silent exam-scope replacement.
findings.resolution: Retain objective 4.8 milestones and explicitly label current operational context; no silent exam-scope replacement.

findings.title: Severity, context and detection ratios needed precise boundaries
findings.evidence: CVSS v4 Supplemental does not alter the numerical score; deployment and exploitation context affect priorities.
findings.recommendation: Add version/vector guidance and an invented prioritization case; separately calculate precision and recall without inventing a false-positive rate.
findings.resolution: Add version/vector guidance and an invented prioritization case; separately calculate precision and recall without inventing a false-positive rate.

findings.title: Location context is not an independent substitute for authentication factors
findings.evidence: Current NIST authentication guidance distinguishes fraud/context signals from an authentication factor and sets scoped password requirements.
findings.recommendation: Explain the exam terminology alongside current context, length, compromise and recovery guidance.
findings.resolution: Explain the exam terminology alongside current context, length, compromise and recovery guidance.
